title: Regional session-open overreaction reversal on 15m: buy a large drop in the first 90 minutes of Tokyo, London or New York

source.title: Intraday price reversals for index futures in the US and Hong Kong (Fung, Mok, Lam, Journal of Banking and Finance 2000)

rule_summary: Timeframe 15m, closed bars; signal at a bar close, fill at the next bar open. Long only, one position. OPEN WINDOWS (6 bars = 90 minutes each): Tokyo = 00:00-01:30 UTC every day; London = 08:00-09:30 London local time, Mon-Fri; New York = 09:30-11:00 New York local time, Mon-Fri (local times converted to UTC with the standard UK/US daylight-saving rules). For window W on day d: r = close of its 6th bar / open of its 1st bar - 1; A = mean of |r| of the same window over its previous 20 occurrences (same session, earlier days only). ENTRY at the close of the 6th bar if r <= -1.0*A AND r <= -0.006 AND no position is open; buy at the next open. Store P0 = open of the window's 1st bar and L = lowest low of the 6 window bars. EXIT at the first of: (a) a bar closes >= P0 (full retrace of the opening drop); (b) a bar closes < L*0.995 (stop); (c) 24 bars (6 hours) after entry, sell at the next open. Windows that start while a position is open are ignored.
mechanism: Fung, Mok and Lam (2000) find intraday reversals after large opening moves in S&P 500 and Hang Seng futures, growing with the size of the opening move and not explained by spreads or panic. Grant, Wolf and Yu (2005, J. Banking & Finance, Montclair page) confirm opening overreaction over 15 years. Counterparty: traders who must execute at a session open (stop and margin orders accumulated while their home market slept, hedgers, desks rebalancing to the overnight move) demand liquidity in a burst; liquidity providers charge for absorbing it, and the price snaps back once the burst is done. Crypto has the same clock-driven order bursts at regional opens (periodic volume and volatility peaks documented in arXiv 2109.12142). Requiring a drop of at least 0.6% and one larger than the window's typical move puts the target (the window open) well above the 0.30-0.45% round trip.
